messages.message:
cleanup: remove LS2K bring-up markers from filesystem and ABI paths


One board's first-boot instrumentation had been left switched on inside the
architecture-neutral paths: six uart_putc calls in the readiness scan that
poll(2) blocks on, eleven in linux_poll itself, and one per syscall in the
dispatch path.  All eighteen were gated on CONFIG_BOARD_LS2K1000 &&
CONFIG_COOPERATIVE_BOOT, so they cost nothing on any other board -- but they
put a board name in code that has no business knowing one, and 0xC0000000-style
debug tracing inside poll(2) is the kind of thing that gets left switched on
by accident and then blamed for a latency problem.

The gating meant the markers were also load-bearing documentation of intent:
they showed where the LS2K1000 bring-up was stuck.  What replaces them is not
nothing -- CONFIG_LS2K_TRAP_TRACE still works for anyone who wants to
re-enable tracing, and kernel/arch/loongarch64/{boot/switch.S,trap/trap.S} keep
their single-character switch/trap checkpoints.  Those are assembly, guarded
by the same CONFIG_BOARD_LS2K1000 test, and they poke the LS2K UART directly
rather than calling into C, so they are legitimately arch-internal and left
alone.  Note the build never actually defined CONFIG_LS2K_TRAP_TRACE, so that
assembly path was already dormant.

The C-side tracing helper uart_trace_ls2k_syscall() in uart.h existed only to
serve the dispatch site and went with it; uart.h no longer mentions any board.

Verified: kernel-only builds clean under -Werror for all nine board targets,
including ls2k1000 itself -- the board the markers were for -- with
DRIVER_DEPLOYMENT=embedded.  check-smp-platform-boundary,
check-concurrency-foundation, check-honesty-policy and check-doc-test-gates
pass.

messages.message:
panic: route LoongArch register dumps through architecture hooks


panic() and the return-to-user path in proc_task_first_entry() read
LoongArch CSRs inline: nine in the panic capture and eight at every first
switch back to user, all behind CONFIG_BOARD_LS2K1000.  That put a board
name and a LoongArch CSR number list inside two architecture-neutral files,
and the CSR reads in panic() ran before va_start purely so the values
survived long enough to print.

Two optional hooks now carry it.  arch_panic_dump() is called from panic()
where the LoongArch block used to print, and arch_debug_dump_user_state()
from the switch path; the generic callers say nothing about which registers
exist.  An architecture opts in by defining ARCH_HAS_BOOT_TRACE_DUMPS in its
own arch/<arch>/include/arch.h, following the ARCH_HAS_* convention the tree
already uses for capability negotiation.  Only loongarch64 does, and only when
CONFIG_DEBUG_BOOT_TRACE is set -- the same flag that compiles the new file --
so every other build gets a no-op inline rather than a declared function with
no definition.  The default has to be an inline and not a weak symbol: a
no-op definition would still be a real call in the panic path.

The switch is now opt-in rather than implicit.  It used to be gated on
CONFIG_BOARD_LS2K1000, which meant a new board could not ask for these dumps
without editing kernel/core/panic.c.  The Makefile sets the flag for the
LS2K1000 cooperative profile, which is the only configuration that had it.

kernel/proc/task.c also had ls2k_dump_user_pt_path(), a page-table walker
written entirely in arch-neutral page-table terms -- arch_pt_vpn,
arch_pte_is_leaf, arch_pte_to_ptr -- behind that board guard.  It is now
dump_user_pt_path() behind CONFIG_DEBUG_BOOT_TRACE, since that is what it
actually is.

CSR numbers are immediates, not a function argument.  Passing the number in a
register let GCC allocate the same register for destination and source,
emitting `csrrd $r8, $r8`, which this assembler rejects; the inline reads this
replaced all used immediates and are kept that way.

Verified: all thirteen board targets build clean under -Werror, and ls2k1000
builds both with DEBUG_BOOT_TRACE (the eleven diagnostics present) and without
(it compiled out).  check-smp-platform-boundary, check-concurrency-foundation,
check-driver-core-model, check-honesty-policy and check-doc-test-gates pass.

sched: query the board for its timer device


idle_loop() tested CONFIG_BOARD_LS2K1000 four times.  Two of those were not
logging: the idle path skipped arch_local_irq_enable() entirely and called
cpu_relax() in place of the arch_idle_wait() sequence.  A board that needs a
different idle strategy therefore had to edit kernel/proc/proc.c, and the only
example of that need in the tree was expressed as a board name in the
scheduler.

board_config_t gains idle_cannot_sleep, and idle_loop() reads it once.  The
polarity is deliberate: every other field in that struct is a pointer, so a
static initializer leaves this one at 0, which means 0 has to be "the timer
works" or every board that does not mention it would silently stop sleeping
and burn a core spinning.  The LS2K1000 sets it only under
CONFIG_COOPERATIVE_BOOT, which is what the old guard tested too -- the same
board in its normal profile still sleeps.

kernel/proc/fork.c's non-preemptive clone launch was left alone.  It looks like
the same problem but is guarded by CONFIG_COOPERATIVE_BOOT, a build profile
rather than a board name, so no board is named in neutral code there and
nothing needs to change.

eleven other board targets are unregressed -- with idle_cannot_sleep zeroed by
static initialization, which is the case that would have broken them if the
polarity were the other way round.  check-smp-platform-boundary,
check-concurrency-foundation, check-driver-core-model, check-honesty-policy and

messages.message:
mm, abi: describe physical address width as a hardware property


Nine sites in architecture-neutral files branched on CONFIG_<architecture> or
CONFIG_BOARD_<name>.  In every case the thing being branched on was a
hardware or firmware property, and writing the architecture's name instead
meant that adding an architecture to the tree silently changed behaviour
nobody had decided on.

Seven are architecture properties and now say so.  Each is a capability macro
in core/arch.h, defaulting to the safe or common case, following the ARCH_HAS_*
convention already in the tree:

  ARCH_EXE_LEAF_RETAIN_UNSAFE   x86_64, loongarch64
  ARCH_FAULT_AROUND_UNSAFE      loongarch64
  ARCH_INSN_FAULT_UNRECOVERABLE ppc64le
  ARCH_TIMER_FREQ_RUNTIME       riscv64
  ARCH_FAST_CURRENT             riscv64
  ARCH_HW_SINGLE_STEP           x86_64
  ARCH_LINUX_EPOLL_EVENT_PACKED x86_64

The first one is a latent bug fix.  mm/fault.c's comment said "LoongArch64 and
x86_64 additionally keep ALL executable private leaves on the anonymous-copy
path" while the code tested only CONFIG_X86_64, so LoongArch64 was taking the
opposite branch from the one its own comment described.  It now sets the
macro.  The change is unobservable on LoongArch64 because
ARCH_FAULT_AROUND_UNSAFE already forces fault_around to 0 there and
direct_private requires fault_around, so what actually changes is that the
comment and the code agree.

The other two are board facts, not architecture facts, and went into
board_config_t next to idle_cannot_sleep rather than into arch.h:

  vdso_user_timer_unreliable  VisionFive 2
  uart_rx_is_polled            VisionFive 2, LS2K1000 cooperative

Both are about how a board's firmware hands over -- whether U-mode can read
the time CSR, whether the console UART has an interrupt -- and neither is a
property of the instruction set.  They replace three CONFIG_BOARD tests: one in
mm/vdso.c and two in drivers/char/uart.c that were keyed on VisionFive 2, and a
third in uart.c that was keyed on the LS2K1000 cooperative profile and is the
same fact as the other two.  As with idle_cannot_sleep the polarity is chosen so
that a static initializer's 0 is the working behaviour.

Verified: all thirteen board targets build clean under -Werror, and ls2k1000
builds under COOPERATIVE_BOOT as well, which is the configuration that exercises
two of the three new flags.  check-smp-platform-boundary,
check-concurrency-foundation, check-driver-core-model, check-abi-boundary,
check-honesty-policy and check-doc-test-gates pass.

messages.message:
mm: reject exec faults outside the VMA permissions


A page fault on a present leaf was answered from the PTE alone: if the leaf
carried PTE_X the exec fault was reported as handled, whatever the VMA said.
That makes a leaf whose execute bit disagrees with its VMA silently
self-fulfilling. On aarch64 the disagreement is not merely bookkeeping --
arch_pte_leaf() derives the hardware UXN/PXN pair from PTE_X, so a stack page
whose leaf picked up a stray X bit really is executable at EL0, mksh jumps
into it, the retry succeeds, the PC does not move to anything meaningful, and
the same stack address faults again immediately.

That is what the post-fork hang was: ~23k prefetch aborts at a stack address
with no kernel output at all, because every round trip returned "handled"
and so no fault was ever reported. It looked like a lost wakeup and behaved
like a livelock; the machine only stopped when the harness timed out.

The VMA is the authority on what an address may be used for, not the PTE, so
cross-check it under mm->lock and refuse an exec fault on a VMA without
VM_EXEC (or write on one without VM_WRITE). The leaf may then be as wrong as
it likes and the worst outcome is the correct one: a clean SIGSEGV naming a
mapping the process was never allowed to execute.

The two demand-fault refusals in the same commit close the matching holes on
the not-present side: an instruction fault inside the stack-growth or brk
window was satisfied with a fresh read/write anon leaf, which has the same
non-advancing-PC property. A stack or heap page is never executable, so those
now fail instead.

aarch64 now reports the crash it was hiding:
  SIGSEGV: pid=5 code=32 sepc=0x3ff0c6e0 ra=0x3ff0c6e0 (a stack address)
  FATAL: pid=5 signal=11 comm=mksh pc=0x3ff0c6e0
instead of spinning until the harness kills it.

MM_PT_META_ENTRIES，也就是"一个策略参数"其实是页帧剩下的余数。7 是对的，
因为 Sv39 的节点页有 512 项；riscv32 有 1024 项，7 × 1024 = 7176 越过一帧，
静态断言直接拒绝编译——一个按单一架构调好的常数，在别的架构上是编译错误。
为了让宽度涨到 8 而删掉 segtab 自己的引用计数（4104 = 4096 + 8），
已经是为迁就布局而删生命周期字段了。

现在 arr 走 slab，idx 是一次 kcalloc(1, sizeof(st) + ENTRIES * NAMES) 的
尾部：没有第二次分配，也就没有第二条失败路径。segtab_detach_locked() 从
pfa_free(virt_to_pfn(st)) 变成 kfree(st)，被标注的 PT 页不再白占一整个 4 KiB
去装 3584 字节索引。sizeof(mm_segtab_t) <= 4096 那条断言随之删除——结构体
不再是页帧大小，它不对应任何真实约束，留着会让人以为还有。

的同一次运行里打印 full_by_level=[0,0,0]。补上之后是 level 1: 749、
level 2: 3169、根层一次都没有——损失不在根表那四个槽位，在 2 MiB 条目塞了

直方图也改成按层逐行打印，8 个层级里此前被静默丢掉的 3..7 现在可见。

PT 页多背 16 KiB。

而那次缺页紧接着就会调 mm_mmap_seg_label() 重新标注——"漏掉的那部分"
第一次缺页之后本来就补上了。看起来像泄漏、实际是已有机制在兜底。

决定性的一次数值：回退路径补完标注后立刻重查同一地址，
relabel_ok=782 relabel_fail=0。补标注每次都成功，792 次回退是 792 个"第一次"，
之后同一映射上每次缺页都走页表名。也就是说这批回退不随工作负载增长，
它等于"被创建过的映射数"这个常量。再往上优化就是在压一个不增长的常量。

据此否决叶表标注：它能把 792 压到 260（降幅 67%，纸面最大），
但代价是每张叶表 2 KiB、1 GiB 工作集 1 MiB、4 GiB 4 MiB——
用不增长的量换随内存增长的量，方向是反的。更要紧的是它换不来简化：
叶表标注要回答"这一页属于哪个映射"，而 cls[] 已经在回答，
等于把刚删掉的 vma_index[] 换个位置请回来，只是这次住在页表里。
CortenMM 的论点正是每 PTE 元数据是唯一权威、不需要第二个命名结构。

结论：宽度 32 是终点。下一步不在分辨率上，而在删掉回退路径本身——
只要回退还在，mm->mmap 就还不能删，迁移就没有真正完成。
这是唯一同时降低复杂度并且降低回退率的方向。

顺带把 alone/shared 拆分记进文档（252/530）：alone 是"标注压根没发生"，
提高分辨率帮不上忙；shared 是"条目挤不下名字"，只有这一类分辨率能收。
能问对这个问题本身就是更正根层那处错误带来的。

三处同步更正：roadmap §13.20.1、testing-gates 的读法说明、
pt.h 里同一句话的注释（它原本把一个错读写成了头文件级的不变量）。

messages.message:
fix: repair x86_64 boot, server image sizing, and MM mapping references


四个互相独立的回归，都是近期改动带进来的。

1) x86_64 一启动就 KERNEL OOPS（pc=kernel_main+0x1f1，BADV=0x0）

   boot/ldscript.ld 里的 `_stack_end = .` 遮蔽了 entry.S 中真正的标签，把
   BSP 启动栈放到了 _bss_end 之上的 ALIGN(16) 处。_bss_end 往上的内存归物理
   页帧分配器所有（mm_init 把 va_to_pa(_bss_end) 交给 pfa_init，后者从
   ROUND_UP(kernel_end, 64) 开始 memset 自己那几 MB 的帧元数据位图），于是
   栈刚用上就被清掉。lwIP 启用 512 KiB ram_heap（MEMP_MEM_MALLOC=1）后
   ram_heap 落在 .bss 末尾，压在栈上，net_init() 里 mem_init() 的哨兵正好落在
   它的活动栈上，下一次 printf 就返回到 kernel_main 的 call *%rax 中间。

   栈改为放进专有的 .bss.stack 段，由 ldscript 在 .bss 里最先收集，因此位于
   .bss 底部且在 _bss_end 之下；另加三条 ASSERT 锁住这个约束。同一处修正
   riscv64/riscv32/loongarch64/loongarch32/ppc64le/vf2：它们的
   `*(.bss.stack)` 排在 `*(.bss .bss.*)` 通配之后，而 ld 只认第一条匹配指令，
   那行一直是死代码。另外 ppc64le 距 pfa memset 边界只有 0 字节余量，现为 12 MB。

2) server-riscv64 镜像装不下（mkfs.ext4: Could not allocate block）

   GUI_MEDIA 把 535 MiB 的 Minecraft 数据注入了每一个 world，包括没有 JVM、
   没有启动器、world_size_mb=512 的 server 镜像。改为只对桌面 world 注入，
   并在 mkrootfs.py 里加装盘前的体积预检，让这类错误直接指名道姓，而不是伪装
   成磁盘满。

3) 凡是声明了端口转发的实例都起不来

   QEMU 9 弃用、QEMU 10 直接拒绝裸的 `tcp::2222-:22` 短写法。清单里仍保留
   可读的短写法，改写集中到 NetCfg.qemu_hostfwd() 一处完成。

4) xfce-x86_64 桌面启动到 dbus-uuidgen 时 use-after-free

   mm_pt_lookup_seg_rcu() 在“同一页表项下两个映射都认领该地址”的歧义分支上对
   一个借来的指针调用了 mm_seg_put()——segtab_seg() 是纯借用，引用归节点共享
   数组所有（segtab_slot() 取得）。成功分支上的 mm_seg_get() 是对的，歧义分支
   漏了对应的一次 put，于是偷走持有者的最后一个引用：第一次故障释放掉页面表
   仍在引用的记录，第二次故障读已释放内存，magic=0 而 panic。删掉这次 put 即可，
   引用计数本就按 slot 配平（annotate 时 get，segtab_entry_forget() 与 segarr
   拆除时 put）。

   同时补上 mm_insert_vma() 两个合并分支里缺失的 mm_mmap_seg_retire()：这是
   唯一会把映射移出链表却不注销标注的改动路径（unmap/split/mprotect 都有）。
   2 MiB 的页表项远粗于映射，ld.so 映射同一共享对象的相邻段时，survivor 长回去
   覆盖被吸收的那半，于是那一项同时指向两个记录，落在被吸收半边的故障就必然歧义。

   引入于 7e6cc1a7e，与 SMP 无关：smp=1/2/4 均稳定复现，同一进程同一 pid。

顺带修掉 arm32 的编译中断：mm_pt_core_init() 与两个 dispatch 计数器原先都在
pt.h/pt.c 的 ARCH_HAS_PGTABLE_OPS 守卫内，而 arm32 按设计不带这个宏
（它有自己的短描述符页表后端），于是 mm.c:50 与 fault.c 的两处引用符号不存在。
计数器是统计量而非能力，移到守卫外让它们在每个构建里都存在；它们的上报点
sys_proc.c 本就自带守卫，arm32 只是不打印。

fix: restore NOMMU builds and missing RISC-V 32-bit syscall numbers


上一修提交把 mm 层的引用计数溢出修掉之后，跑实例矩阵又挖出两处编译中断，
都与"NOMMU/32 位下某个头文件守卫把不该藏的东西藏了"这一类有关。

1) 三个 qemu-*-nommu 实例根本编译不过

   pt.h 用 `#if defined(ARCH_HAS_PGTABLE_OPS) && !defined(CONFIG_NOMMU)` 圈住了
   一批声明，可引用它们的代码却没跟着藏：

   - mm/cow.c 整份实现（含 mm_fork_clone_range / mm_fork_clone_present_range）
     无条件调用 mm_pt_leaf_table / mm_pt_peek / mm_pt_sync_status；
   - mm/fault.c 的 cow_sync_status() 与 shadow_seg_check() 同样如此。两者的调用点
     本来就在 NOMMU 分支里，只有定义漏了守卫；
   - mm/fault.c:429 那句 handle_demand_fault_attempt() 的前向声明是全局的，而定义
     与唯一的调用点都在 #ifndef CONFIG_NOMMU 里，于是 NOMMU 下 -Werror 报
     "declared static but never defined"；
   - 最根本的一处：mm_seg_get() / mm_seg_put() 连声明带定义都关在守卫里。这两个是
     slab 对象上的引用计数，与页表毫无关系，而 vma.c 在未受守卫的路径上增减引用，
     于是 NOMMU 下调用的是不存在的函数。

   cow.c 的处理是补一组返回 0 的实现而不是删函数：mm_fork() 在 mm/vm.c 里只在
   返回值为负时判失败，而那两处调用点没有守卫，删掉照样编不过；NOMMU 地址空间是
   平的，本来就没有页表可克隆、没有写保护可降，返回 0 是诚实的答案。

   mm_seg_get/put 移到守卫外，与 dispatch 计数器同样处理：它们是统计/计数，不是
   能力，声明跟着定义走，vma.c 才有的调用才有着落。

   三个 NOMMU 内核（aarch64 / riscv64 / riscv32）现已全部编译通过。

   注意：编译通过之后它们在早期启动里暴露出另一个问题——page_cache_init() 经
   page_cache_grow_internal() 调 kcalloc() 时触发缺页 panic。这是被上面这层编译
   错误挡在后面的既有缺陷，不是本次改动引入的（本次没有碰 slab.c 或 page_cache.c，
   而 NOMMU 此前根本无法编译、也就无从运行）。NOMMU 的 slab/页缓存尚不能工作，
   本次未修。

2) riscv32 用户态编译不过

   musl 的 riscv32 头文件沿用上游 riscv32 Linux 的编号，而本内核的 riscv32 没有
   专属 syscall_nr 头（只有 arm32 和 x86_64 有），走的是 include/core/syscall_nr.h
   这张通用表。两者对不上的地方，用户态直接调 syscall() 的代码就编不过：

   - 先撞上的是 pselect6 / ppoll（上游 riscv32 只有 _time64 变体，musl 的内部
     shim 会把缺省的 SYS_pselect6 顶到 _time64，但 cmds/stress/poll_edge.c 包含的
     是公开的 <sys/syscall.h>，shim 根本不生效）；
   - 修掉后又依次撞上 timer_gettime / timer_settime。

   查全树之后，把 user/cmds 真正用到、而 riscv32 头文件没有、又确实存在于内核表里
   的名字一次性补齐：pselect6、ppol、renameat、timer_gettime、timer_settime、
   clock_gettime、close_range、io_getevents、time、utimes。编号一律照抄
   kernel/include/core/syscall_nr.h —— 内核派发认的是这张表，照抄上游的号能编过，
   但调到的会是别的系统调用。

   SYS_mkswap 与 a20_* 没有放进 musl：那些是 A20OS 自有的，用户态是通过直接包含
   内核头拿到的（如 cmds/core/mkswap.c 包含 kernel/include/mm/swap.h）。

   riscv32 用户态现在能编过 musl 与全部 cmds，最后停在
   `native-handle-rv32` 需要 riscv32-linux-gnu-gcc，而本机没装这个交叉工具链——
   与 arm32、loongarch32 缺工具链同属环境问题。

messages.message:
mm: expose /proc/<pid>/auxv and accept PROT_BTI and PROT_MTE in mprotect


两处都为接入 FEX（aarch64 宿主上的 x86 翻译器）铺路，内核侧到此不再
是阻塞项；通道本身（exec_try_translator 改写 bprm 后原生 re-exec）零改动。

/proc/<pid>/auxv：此前完全没有该节点，auxv 只在内核构造初始栈时存在。
不在读取时从栈回读——那段内存归程序所有、随时可能被覆写，回读回答的是
「读者内存里现在有什么」而非「这个镜像当初如何被 exec」。故在 exec 时
把向量拷进 mm_struct_t，由 /proc 重放；跨 fork 继承无需额外代码，因为
mm_fork 的 *child = *parent 已带过去，这也是用值数组而非指针的原因。
A20 native ABI 用 a20_start_info_t 启动、本就不发布 auxv，故其 auxv_n
保持 0、节点读出为空——对一个从未被交给 auxv 的程序这是正确的。

PROT_BTI/PROT_MTE：旧的 prot & ~(R|W|X) 把这两个位当未知位退回 EINVAL。
要害在于它们与访问权同处一个参数，调用方无法「去掉它们重试」，只能拿到
一个无法解释的 EINVAL。改为在 mprotect 入口即剥掉（prot &= ~PROT_HINT_MASK），
位置在 W^X 策略与页表之前，使两处重读 prot 时只看到 R/W/X、hint 不会被
误当权限。真正未知的位仍照常 EINVAL，校验未整体放松。mmap 本就不校验

messages.message:
net: fix loopback TCP stalls caused by close-time RST and dropped staged data


tcp_loopback_test 在 tcpmode=lwip 下稳定失败：握手完成、服务端 send(2)
返回 2，客户端 read() 却拿到 0（EOF）。用临时探针跑 a20.tcpmode=lwip
（4 CPU）取到证据链：

  SRV: recv=18 ok=1 send=2 closed
  [DIAG] recv_cb s=<client> len=2      <- lwIP 已把 2 字节交给 socket 层
  [DIAG] bh ring s=<client> len=2 closed=1
  CLI: recv=0                            <- 数据在 bottom half 里被扔了

两处缺陷叠加：

1) net_inet_socket_destroy() 对已建立的 pcb 无条件 tcp_abort()。那是
   tcp_abandon(pcb, 1)，会把 RST 放上线，等于告诉对端"丢掉我发的东西"。
   服务端做的是最普通的 write(); close()，最后一段数据被这一行 routine
   地毁掉，对端能不能看见取决于 RST 和数据谁先到接收队列。改成先解绑
   回调再 tcp_close()，ERR_MEM 时才退回 tcp_abort()——与 net_tcp_close_pcb()
   同一形状。

2) net_inet_bottom_half_process_socket_locked() 先处理 bh_error/bh_closed
   再 drain bh_ring，而 ring 的 `if (!s->closed)` 守卫于是把 lwIP 已经交付
   的字节一起扔了。TCP 在同一趟 bottom half 里交付数据和紧随其后的 FIN，
   于是 read() 对一个还欠着数据的连接回答 EOF。改成先把两个标志 capture
   到局部变量、drain 完再按序施加；守卫重新只对"本地已 close"的 socket
   生效——那才是它本来要防的东西。RST 跟在数据后面到达时同理，且更糟。

修 (1) 暴露出一个此前被 (1) 掩盖的缺陷：优雅关闭会留 TIME_WAIT pcb，而
SO_REUSE 在本树是 opt.h 的默认 0，socket 层的 reuseaddr 又从未搬上 pcb，
于是 tcp_bind() 照旧扫 TIME_WAIT 表，同端口重启一律 EADDRINUSE(98)——
第一次运行 PASS、之后每次 bind 失败。lwipopts.h 打开 SO_REUSE=1，
net_inet_tcp_apply_options() 把 reuseaddr 搬成 SOF_REUSEADDR（accept 子
pcb 经 SOF_INHERITED 继承），setsockopt 在 socket 层把新值推回已存在的
pcb（它发生在 socket() 与 bind() 之间）。登记见 DIVERGENCE.md §2.6。

证据（ARCH=riscv64 ABI=linux BRINGUP=0 NR_CPUS=4 dev-build，QEMU，
a20.tcpmode=lwip）：
- 基线（仅 item1）：端口 12345 连跑 3 次 3 PASS、连跑 10 次 0 PASS，
  每次 CLI: recv=0；改用 6 个不同端口仍是 0/6 PASS
- 本提交：同端口连跑 8 次 8 PASS，CLI: recv=2 data=ok
- make smoke-network-suite: PASS（TCP_ACCEPT/TCP_LOOPBACK/UDP_LOOPBACK/
  ICMP_LOOPBACK 全 PASS）

messages.message:
net: return EPIPE after peer reset instead of ENOTSOCK


tcp_edge_test 的 epipe 场景要求 send() 在对端 reset 后返回 EPIPE。
在上一提交（回环传输修复）之后它稳定失败，报 errno=88 (ENOTSOCK)。

用临时 printf 探针取到确切状态（a20.tcpmode=lwip，4 CPU）：

  [DIAG] net_sendto_sock fallthrough: dom=2 type=1 conn=1 closed=1
         ever=1 tcp=0x0
  TCP_EDGE_TEST: epipe send errno=88 (Not a socket)

type=1 是 SOCK_STREAM、ever_connected=1，而 tcp=0x0——说明这不是"不是套接字"，
而是一条被 lwIP 拆掉的连接。原因在派发条件本身：

  if ((s->domain == AF_INET || s->domain == AF_INET6) &&
      (s->udp || s->raw || s->tcp))
      return net_inet_sendto(...);

它按"当前是否持有 pcb"来路由。lwip_tcp_err_cb() 在 RST 和每一个致命错误上
都会把 s->tcp 置 NULL，所以 s->tcp == NULL 恰恰是一条死掉的 TCP 连接的常态。
这些 write 因此绕过 net_inet_sendto() 掉进下面的通用"两个套接字"路径，
由 net_socket_is_live() 判定 s->closed 而返回 ENOTSOCK——对一个货真价实的
fd 谎称它不是套接字。

改成按套接字类型判定，并显式豁免 fast 路径：fast 模式的套接字按设计就不持有
pcb、由下面的快捷路径服务，所以这个豁免必须写出来而不是靠默认。语义沿用
net_inet_send_tcp() 已有的 Linux ABI 规则：ever_connected 则 EPIPE，否则
ENOTCONN。sys_sendto 与 write(2) 两条派发路径（net_sendto_sock、
net_vfile_write）都有同一个缺陷，一并修。

这不是上一提交引入的缺陷：基线上 epipe 能过，是因为它失败在 partial-io 上
（3 次连跑只有 2 次过），且基线的顺序恰好让 s->tcp 在 send() 到达派发时还没被
置空。上一提交把 close() 从 abort 改成优雅关闭，改变了 RST 与 send 的先后，
把这个一直存在的窗口变成了稳定命中。证据：同一探针在基线上不打印任何 DIAG，
而基线的 epipe 自身也不稳定。

证据（ARCH=riscv64 ABI=linux BRINGUP=0 NR_CPUS=4 dev-build，QEMU，
a20.tcpmode=lwip）：
- tcp_edge_test 连跑 3 次：修前 2/3（失败形态是 partial-io），修后 3/3
- 跨模式切换 lwip → fast → lwip 各跑一次 tcp_edge_test：两次实际执行均 PASS
- make smoke-network-suite: PASS，11 passed / 1 declared-absent，
  含 TCP_ACCEPT / TCP_LOOPBACK / TCP_EDGE / UDP_LOOPBACK / ICMP_LOOPBACK

net: add scatter-gather fallback and driver capability reporting


a20_lwip_register_netifs() 采样一次 ops->caps(dev) 存进
a20_lwip_netif_state_t::caps；a20_lwip_linkoutput() 只在
(caps & NET_DEV_CAP_TX_SG) && ops->send_sg && p->next == NULL 三个条件
同时成立时走 send_sg()，其余情况逐字节回到原来的 pbuf_copy_partial()
-> netfilter_output() -> send() 线性路径。

为什么只取单段：netfilter_output() 的形参是平坦帧指针
(netfilter.c:512)，它要从 Ethernet/VLAN/IPv4/L4 里就地解端口和地址，

（kernel/include/drvmod/drvmod.h:31 的 512 KiB）。256 项 x 2048 字节 x 两

环变成 kmalloc 之后 sizeof 不再等于项数，两处都改成显式的
E1000_RING_SIZE。

多缓冲帧不再直接丢。旧代码在 !EOP 时把 length 清零，等于丢掉每个超过
2048 字节的帧的第一片；更糟的是它照样把这一项交还给设备，RDT 就停在帧
中间，下一次读从半个包开始。现在从 rx_next 走到 EOP，把各片线性拼进调用
者的缓冲：每一片都在清 status 之前先把 DD/EOP/errors/length 读出来（EOP
就在即将被清零的那个字节里），交付与否都退役该描述符，RDT 写的是本次
退役的最后一个而不是 last+1——那正是每次环回绕丢一个包的经典差一错误。
出错时整帧退役并返回 0，而不是把设备标记为坏的前缀交给上层。遍历上界是
环大小：设备永不置 EOP 的情形代价是一整个环然后在描述符边界上重新同步。

82574L 简单接收中断节流。ITR (0x000C) 只在 e1000 这一代部件的寄存器组里
存在，82540EM/82545EM/82546EB/82541PI 在这里是保留空洞，所以
e1000_itr_init() 按 device id == 0x10D3 门控写入，而不是无条件写。节流
在这里安全而不是吞吐下降：中断触发的接收排空是无界的——
e1000_irq_handler() 把 netif 下标交给 a20_lwip_process_netif_irq_locked()，
后者以 0 预算调 a20_lwip_process_netif_rx_tx_locked(n, 0)，一次中断排空整
个环。间隔只改变多久排空一次，不改变每次排空多少，256 项又给了一次突发量
设了上界。取 3904 x 1024 ns ≈ 3.9 ms：节流的代价是收包要等下一次中断，

messages.message:
feat: add kernel preemption behind CONFIG_KERNEL_PREEMPT


Cooperative kernel code can now lose the CPU at a hardware-interrupt
return: after arch_handle_irq() completes, kernel_preempt_at_irq_return()
switches out the interrupted task when need_resched is pending, the task
is RUNNING and not idle, and the interrupted context ran with interrupts
enabled (per-arch ARCH_IRQ_WAS_ENABLED_IN_TRAP against the saved status
register).  The resume path needs no new assembly: the preempted task's
kstack still holds its trap frame under the handler frames, so __switch
back into it unwinds through the ordinary IRQ epilogue.

Two invariants make the per-CPU preempt counter sound without per-task
save/restore: sched() masks interrupts across pick->publish->__switch
(each task restores its own flag state at out:, because __switch already
saves/restores flags per task), and context_switch_locked() panics if
ever entered with the counter raised -- a voluntary switch under a
spinlock was already banned by the lock contract, this makes it a checked
fact.  spin_lock/spin_unlock/spin_trylock_irqsave now bracket every
critical section with preempt_disable/enable; waiting for a lock stays
preemptible.

Hosted arches get the hook by default; the MCU profile (armv7m PendSV)
keeps its cooperative scheduler, and a hosted build missing the hook is
a compile error rather than a silent never-preempts.

Also: ppc64le trap dispatch learned to route kernel-mode traps to
kernel_trap_handler() by SRR1[PR] (previously every trap took the user
path, so kernel ticks were charged as user time and the preemption point
was unreachable), and BUILD_VARIANT gains -preempt so pre-merge build
directories cannot be reused with stale no-preemption objects.

cow.c guards its per-PTE status sidecar calls with ARCH_HAS_PGTABLE_OPS
(arm32's short-descriptor backend has none) so the arm32 build gets past
mm/fork again.

Verification: check-*-bringup for x86_64, riscv64, aarch64, riscv32,
loongarch64, ppc64le; smoke-* for the same six; smoke-smp-bringup;
smoke-abi-linux; RT-wakeup A/B probe (user/cmds/core/preempt_lat.c)
under TCG on x86_64 and riscv64, smp=1 and smp=2 pinned and unpinned:
max wakeup 557ms -> 21ms (x86_64 smp1), 1ms (x86_64 smp2), 427ms -> 31ms
(riscv64 smp1), 10ms (riscv64 smp2) against preempt-off controls.

messages.message:
net: add a runtime probe for the lock contract and record its refcount findings


docs/net/network-lock-contract.md listed, as the largest gap between the lock
contract and the implementation, that only the g_lwip_lock half was executable.
LWIP_ASSERT_CORE_LOCKED() had been wired to a panicking probe in 7d217d3fd;
the net locks had nothing.  Two rules were prose only:

  - net_sock_lock2() takes two sockets in ascending address order, and a
    critical section holds at most two socket locks;
  - a bucket lock is never taken while a socket lock is held (the bucket is the
    outer lock; net_bucket_scan() and the register/unregister pair nest the
    other way, which is the sanctioned direction).

This lands both probes plus the runtime verification impl-notes-net.md §8.2,
§8.3, §8.5, §8.6 and §8.7 recorded as never run.

net-lock probe (kernel/net/net_lock_probe.c, new)
--------------------------------------------------
A per-CPU set of the net locks this CPU holds, checked on every acquire:
duplicate (a self-deadlock the spinlock reports with no explanation), socket
lock out of address order, a third socket lock, a bucket lock under a socket
lock, and a second bucket lock (net_bucket_lock2() was deleted in 7c7a4d7c8, so
one is the ceiling).

Per-CPU rather than per-task is the right granularity and the reason is load
bearing: every net lock is spin_lock_irqsave()/spin_unlock_irqrestore(), and
net_sock_lock2() takes its second lock with plain spin_lock() only after the
first has disabled interrupts.  Interrupts are therefore off for the whole held
window, so the holder can be neither preempted nor interrupted into a nested
acquire, and cannot migrate while holding one.  If a net lock ever stops being
irqsave, this table stops being authoritative; that is written down at the
definition rather than left for the next reader to infer.

Arming is at the end of net_init() (socket.c), for the reason
g_lwip_lock_armed already documents: before that the registry locks do not
exist.  Rendering is on /proc/net/status next to the lwip row, and a switch-off
build prints "net_lock: not checked" so an absent probe is never read as a
clean one.

CONFIG_NET_LOCK_ASSERT gains a third value: 0 absent, 1 panic on violation, 2
count only.  The counting mode exists because a counting signal trains people to
ignore the line; on a long soak the final count is worth more than a dead
machine on the first hit.

net_socket_registry_init() now compares lock_counters_count() either side of
its registration loop against NET_SOCK_BUCKETS and reports a shortfall, so
"the contention audit covers the net data plane" is a checked statement.

Reference-count ledger
----------------------
impl-notes-net.md §8.3/§8.6 recorded net_socket_ref/free as a primitive walked
by hand over 54 sites and never once executed.  Now:

  - net_socket_free() uses a CAS loop instead of __atomic_fetch_sub().  The
    old form could not tell "dropped the last reference" from "dropped one too
    many": both land on the same atomic.  A non-positive count is now refused
    and counted rather than driving the count negative.
  - A ref_magic canary, set on alloc and cleared by the free that releases the
    object, rejects a free aimed at something that is not a live socket.  Stated
    plainly at the field: obj_cache hands the same address back to the next
    socket, so a double free landing on a *reused* slot stays invisible.  It
    catches the other case, which is the one that happens.
  - allocs / frees / live / faults render on /proc/net/status.  `live` is the
    leak reading: a create/destroy cycle that leaks moves it and not
    syscall-sockets' `open`, which counts only table-visible sockets.

ENOTCONN attribution
--------------------
§8.5's open question was whether the peer-revalidation window is reachable, and
it could not be asked: the window and "this socket was never connected" surface
as the same errno.  All 13 -ENOTCONN return sites now go through net_notconn()
with a reason, four of which are the window, and /proc/net/status prints
`total=` and `window=` separately.

The AF_UNIX over-drop the ledger found
--------------------------------------
With CONFIG_NET_REF_ASSERT=1 the first run panicked on the first AF_UNIX close:

  net_socket_free: canary-mismatch: object was not a live socket
  refs=0 allocs=127 frees=126 faults=1
  net_socket_free <- net_socket_close_file <- vfs_finalize_closed_vfile <- sys_close

Cause: net_socket_unregister() early-returns for a socket with no slot and does
not release a reference, but both generic teardown paths dropped "the registry
reference" unconditionally.  An AF_UNIX accepted child is never registered --
`grep -rn net_register_socket_locked kernel/net/socket_unix.c` has no hits, the
behaviour impl-notes-net.md §3bis(b) records as inherited -- so it carries one
reference, not two.  Every AF_UNIX close therefore freed the socket mid-teardown
and kept dereferencing it: wait_queue_wake_all() on freed wait queues, then a
second free.

This was not introduced here and was not a live memory-safety failure: the old
fetch_sub compared against 1, so the extra free read as -1, matched nothing and
returned.  The object was freed exactly once by accident rather than by design,
and the use-after-free survived because nothing read the freed memory in a way
that faulted.  What changed is that it is now visible.

Fix: net_socket_unregister() returns whether it released a slot, and each caller
drops the registry reference only when it did.  All five call sites updated --
socket_file.c:304 (the fd's own socket, which for an AF_UNIX accepted child is
itself unregistered), socket_file.c:370 (queued children), socket_control.c:393
(accept install failure), socket_inet.c:1235 and :2072 (accept-stage and local
connect rollbacks, where a slot is guaranteed but the shape is made uniform).
Returning "was there a slot" puts the knowledge in the function that released
the thing the reference was counted against, so the pairing cannot drift again.

Evidence on the tree carrying this commit, riscv64 both-dev,
CONFIG_NET_LOCK_ASSERT=1 CONFIG_NET_REF_ASSERT=1, single CPU:
  SOCKET_STRESS: PASS / NET_STRESS_TEST: PASS / UNIX_TEST: PASS
  net_lock: armed=1 violations=0 sites=0 held_cpu0=0 lockcounters_short=0
  net_sock_ref: live=1 allocs=129 frees=128 faults=0
  net_notconn: total=0 window=0 reasons=13
live=1 agrees with "syscall-sockets: open=1" and "lanes: sockets=1" (the DHCP
socket), which is the cross-check the two readings exist for.

Negative controls, so the probe is not vacuous.  A temporary injection that made
the first post-arm bucket acquire look as though a socket lock were already held
produced, under mode 1:
  net lock contract: bucket lock under socket lock ... cpu=0 held=1 violations=1
followed by [PANIC].  A second temporary injection that poisoned the held set
with one synthetic socket lock at a higher address, under mode 2, produced
"net_lock: armed=1 violations=11449 sites=8" with SOCKET_STRESS: PASS -- i.e.
the address-order check fires and mode 2 counts without aborting.  Both
injections were reverted and are not in this commit.  The third-socket-lock
branch shares the reporting path with the address-order branch but was not
separately injected; say so rather than implying three controls for two runs.

docs: record 797 failure-free samples and correct the counting gap


Docs only.  Second amplification round for the residual connect flake in
net-lanes.md, which 2026-10-05 left unresolved at 78 negative samples.

Two rounds, 4 CPU + 4 lane + a20.tcpmode=lwip, CONFIG_NET_PCB_SANE=1 and
CONFIG_NET_LOCK_ASSERT=1 throughout, ten independent boots each, five repeats
of the eight-port set per boot:

  round A   CONFIG_NET_RACE_DELAY_US=500   400 issued / 398 executed / 0 failed
  round B   CONFIG_NET_RACE_DELAY_US=0     400 issued / 399 executed / 0 failed

797 executed, zero failures; 0.98^797 is about 1.1e-7.  That is NOT a claim
that the flake was fixed -- nothing in the implementation was changed for it
this round, and the two historical failures (ports 12404/12405) predate the
current tree.  It is the reading the doc's own next-step rule predicted: the
2% came from an older tree, so the next move is to check the build id of
those two samples rather than keep hunting a race here.  Round A's 500 us is
also *not* beyond the 2000 us already tried last round; what it adds is
sample count, not amplification, and the doc says so rather than letting the
table imply otherwise.

What is new and worth more than the sample count: the console garbles input.
Three of the 800 commands arrived in the guest with adjacent characters
transposed or dropped -- "tcp_accept_test" became "tcp_aceptc_test",
"tpc_accept_test" and "ctp_accept_test" -- and mksh reported
"inaccessible or not found".  The input rate is one line per second and the
host side emitted the bytes correctly, so this is the guest UART receive
path, and it happens before the command runs at all.

That matters for how anyone measures this flake.  grep -c 'TCP_ACCEPT_TEST:
PASS' counts a command that never executed as a command that did not fail,
which silently eats 0.4% of the sample.  smoke-net-tcp-lanes is wrong in the
opposite direction: a swallowed command drops passes to 7 and the gate
reports a failure.  The new table keeps "issued" and "executed" in separate
columns for that reason, and the next-steps list now puts fixing the sample
accounting ahead of moving the amplifier, because without it the remaining
experiments are equally untrustworthy.

Also folded in, all measured on this branch:
  - the two negative controls from impl-notes-net.md 11.3 re-run independently,
    confirming mode 1 panics and mode 2 counts without aborting;
  - the multi-core refcount evidence 11.4 said it lacked: live=1 faults=0
    across all twenty 4-CPU boots, which is what makes "the ledger does not
    leak under real multi-core handshakes" more than a single-CPU reading;
  - the LOCK_COUNTERS_MAX budget question 8.2/8.7 left open, answered on the
    server profile: registered=141 capacity=192 dropped=0, i.e. 128 bucket
    locks plus 13 others, 51 to spare.

net: gate the SIOCSIFMTU ceiling and make the ioctl reach it


a20_lwip_if_set_mtu() has refused an MTU whose frame does not fit the
profile's scratch buffer since the last round, and nothing in the tree had
ever run that line: SIOCSIFMTU was dispatched by net_vfile_ioctl() into
net_vfile_ifreq_ioctl(), which had no A20_SIOCSIFMTU arm and answered
ENOTTY to every caller, so the only live door to the check was
RTM_NEWLINK -- and netlink_test only ever re-applied the MTU the interface
already had, which sits below the ceiling.

Two changes:

  socket_file.c wires SIOCSIFMTU to a20_lwip_if_set_mtu() rather than to a
  bare nif->mtu write.  The RFC 791 floor and the profile's frame ceiling
  are enforced in that one place, and a direct write would be the only way
  to configure an MTU the receive path then truncates at its clamp and the
  transmit path refuses with ERR_BUF.  The int->uint16_t range check is
  here because 0x10000 would otherwise truncate to 0 and be refused as a
  below-minimum MTU instead of as the out-of-range value it is.

  netlink_test discovers the ceiling instead of hardcoding one.  It is per
  profile (498 on the embedded tier's 512 B frame buffer, 1522 on the
  1536 B ones) and userspace cannot read which tier is built, so a
  bisection over the monotonic accept/refuse predicate finds the exact
  boundary, and then both sides are asserted: 65535 refused, ceiling
  accepted, ceiling+1 refused with EINVAL twice, the value read back
  through SIOCGIFMTU, SIOCSIFMTU refusing above and accepting at the
  ceiling, and the original MTU restored.  Discovery is cross-checked
  against the unconditional 65535 refusal, so a kernel with no ceiling at
  all fails rather than passing with a ceiling of 65535.

One existing assertion was profile-1-broken and is fixed here rather than
left: "RTM_NEWLINK re-applying the current MTU is accepted" sent a literal
1500, which on the embedded tier is a request the 498 ceiling refuses.
It read the current MTU now.  It never surfaced as a tier 1 failure only
because the tier 1 suite hangs earlier, in tcp_accept_test.

messages.message:
virtio-net: reassemble MRG_RXBUF frames across real buffers


The feature was acknowledged and num_buffers was read, but a frame could
never span two posted buffers, so the merge loop was unreachable code.

Why it was unreachable is in QEMU, not in the posting shape.  The device
pops one receive element per iteration (hw/net/virtio-net.c:1971), copies at
most what is left of the frame into it (:2023-2025) and loops while
offset < size (:1958); it writes the iteration count -- the number of
elements it popped -- into the header's num_buffers (:2043).  A 1536 B
payload swallowed a 1514 B frame whole, so num_buffers was pinned at 1.
Posting 512 B payloads inverts that: a full-MTU frame spans three, a
minimum frame still spans one, and the merge path runs on ordinary traffic.
The descriptor shape is unchanged from the one measurement already settled
-- header and payload in one descriptor, no NEXT, no context descriptor --
only the payload size moved.

  [VIRTIO-NET0] ready legacy=0 mac=52:54:00:12:34:56 qsize=256 hdr=12 mrg_rxbuf=1 rxbuf=524 offered(mq=0 csum=0 guest_csum=0)
  [VIRTIO-NET0] first frame reassembled from 2 buffers (rxbuf=524)
  /tmp/big64.bin: saved 65536 bytes
  65536 /tmp/big64.bin
  --- 10.0.2.2 ping statistics --- 4 packets transmitted, 4 received

measured under qemu-system-riscv64 10.0.13, guest wget against a host
python3 -m http.server serving a 65536-byte file, then guest
"ping 10.0.2.2 4".  The log line prints the first spanning frame only, and
the first one slirp happened to send was a two-buffer frame; a full-MTU
frame is three by the arithmetic above, which no single log line shows
because the counter behind the line is not exposed over any ioctl.  lwIP verifies the TCP checksum of every merged frame,
so a mis-joined frame cannot reach the socket; 65536 of 65536 bytes and a
4/4 ping with the merge path firing say the join is right.

What does not cover this: make smoke-network-suite passes on the same build
but does not exercise the merge path at all.  It drives loopback plus a
telnetd/DNS handshake, and every frame it exchanges fits inside one 524-byte
buffer, so num_buffers stays 1 and the log carries no reassembly line -- a
green suite is not evidence for this feature and the section in
docs/server-readiness.md now says so.  Conversely the host-to-guest
direction does not work in this slirp setup: ping 10.0.2.15 from the host is
0/4 whatever the boot timing, so the ping evidence above is the guest
pinging the gateway, not the other way round.

That fix exposed a latent bug in the merge loop itself: it subtracted a
virtio_net_hdr from every buffer of the chain, including continuations.
Only the first buffer carries a header -- QEMU resets `total` per element
and adds guest_hdr_len only when i == 0 (hw/net/virtio-net.c:1996-2025:
`if (i == 0)` at :1996, `total += n->guest_hdr_len` at :2016, the payload
copy at :2023) --
so the old code would have dropped the first 12 payload bytes of every
merged frame.  It never showed because no device ever produced a
continuation buffer.

Buffers without MRG_RXBUF keep a whole frame each: the device drops a
frame that does not fit one buffer (hw/net/virtio-net.c:2030-2036), so
small buffers there would be a silent receive black hole.

Ring memory per instance drops from 790 KiB to 534 KiB on a modern device,
or 862 KiB to 606 KiB legacy, counting every region virtio_net_ring_bytes()
adds: the receive stride is 524 rather than 1548, the transmit stride is
unchanged at 1548 (TX never merges), and the descriptor tables, avail/used
rings and bookkeeping arrays are untouched.

messages.message:
e1000: measure receive reassembly across descriptors


e1000_recv() walks the descriptor chain to EOP, but no frame could ever
span two descriptors, so the walk was unexercised.  One thing kept that
true: the device discards every frame past 1514 bytes unless RCTL[5] LPE
is set -- e1000x_is_oversized() compares against header_size + ETH_MTU
when LPE is clear (hw/net/e1000x_common.c:141-152, the drop condition at
:151-153) -- and LPE was clear.

The per-descriptor size is not what made the walk unreachable, and an
earlier draft of this message said so wrongly.  There is no RCTL.BSIZE
field in this model at all: "BSIZE" occurs zero times in QEMU 10.0.13's
hw/net/e1000.c and hw/net/e1000x_common.c, and the only BSIZE masks that
model carries are the PSRCTL parse-and-classify ones (hw/net/e1000_regs.h
:179-187), a different register.  This driver posts legacy descriptors, so
a buffer is exactly the length the guest writes into the descriptor and a
long frame simply walks on to the next one.  E1000_BUF_SIZE = 2048 sets
how many descriptors one frame costs, not whether it can cross one.

So RCTL.LPE is now programmed, with JUMBO set to a ceiling of two buffers
(1514 + 2560 = 4074 bytes of frame, inside 2 * 2048 with the FCS) rather
than the 16 KiB the part can address: two descriptors per frame is the
bound the walk is claimed to meet.  QEMU ignores JUMBO and tests only LPE
against its own 16 * KiB - ETH_FCS_LEN ceiling
(hw/net/e1000x_common.c:147-149), so the register is written for the part's
sake and not because QEMU reads it.

Feeding it a long frame needs a host that can produce one, and the obvious
route is closed.  slirp has no mtu option --

  $ qemu-system-x86_64 -netdev user,id=n0,mtu=9000
  qemu-system-x86_64: -netdev user,id=n0,mtu=9000: Invalid parameter 'mtu'

-- and raw sockets are denied here (uid=1000, SOCK_RAW ->
"[Errno 1] Operation not permitted"), so no frame larger than a 1500-byte
MTU payload can be made to cross slirp at all.
What does work is -netdev socket,id=n0,fd=N with a datagram socketpair
(net/socket.c:706-741 treats one datagram as one frame), driven from an
unprivileged parent process.  Injecting a 2842-byte frame at the guest MAC:

  [E1000] first frame reassembled from 2 descriptors (buf=2048)
  en2      -          5            0            6            0

Before LPE the same injection produced RX-OK 1 (the single-descriptor
control frame) and no reassembly line at all.

What this does NOT establish: an over-long frame is reassembled correctly
and then dropped by lwIP, because the link MTU is
NET_PROFILE_NETIF_MTU = 1500 (kernel/net/net_profile.h:190) and no IPv4
packet above it is deliverable.  End-to-end jumbo needs the profile table
and the pbuf sizing to move together, which is the net stack's, not the
driver's, to change.  Receive-side capability only until then.

messages.message:
docs: explain why checksum-offload capability bits remain disabled


Last round recorded "vendored lwIP 2.2.2 has no flag to carry the checksum
offload handshake", with opt.h:2449-2450 (LWIP_CHECKSUM_ON_COPY default 0)
and the seven netif.h:84-107 NETIF_FLAG_* bits as the evidence.  Half of
that is wrong and the other half is beside the point.

The flag exists.  lwIP 2.2.2 carries ten NETIF_CHECKSUM_GEN_* /
NETIF_CHECKSUM_CHECK_* bits (netif.h:140-153), a netif->chksum_flags field
(netif.h:340-342) and NETIF_SET_CHECKSUM_CTRL() / IF__NETIF_CHECKSUM_ENABLED()
(netif.h:408-417) -- all of it behind LWIP_CHECKSUM_CTRL_PER_NETIF, which
opt.h:2371-2373 defaults to 0, which expands those two macros to nothing and a
netif == NULL check that is always true.  None of that is a NETIF_FLAG_* bit,
which is why counting the seven flags missed it.

LWIP_CHECKSUM_ON_COPY was also cited for the wrong thing.  It governs
accumulating a checksum while copying an application buffer into a pbuf;
pbuf_take() itself is a MEMCPY and never looks at a checksum
(src/core/pbuf.c:1254-1295).  Whether the stack verifies a received frame is
decided by CHECKSUM_CHECK_* in ip4.c:532-533, udp.c:419 and tcp_in.c:166-169.

So the decision not to enable TX/RX checksum offload stands, but the
reason is now three concrete things rather than one wrong one:

  - the TCP send path finalises the segment checksum with no
    IF__NETIF_CHECKSUM_ENABLED() around it at all (tcp_out.c:1587-1596), so
    flipping the switch offloads UDP and leaves TCP computing a full
    checksum anyway -- a half state that is worse than none;
  - lwIP's carrier is one bit per netif, while "this frame was verified" is
    per frame, and this HAL's recv() returns a length and nothing else.  QEMU
    cannot supply the missing half either: VIRTIO_NET_HDR_F_DATA_VALID is
    defined (standard-headers/linux/virtio_net.h:132) but occurs zero times
    in QEMU 10.0.13's hw/net/virtio-net.c, so a virtio-net RX frame never
    carries a verdict to pass on;
  - the NAT path folds new addresses and ports into the L4 checksum
    incrementally (netfilter_nat.c:754-892: netfilter_csum_delta at :754-763,
    netfilter_fix_l4 at :815-834, netfilter_set_port at :875-892), which is
    arithmetic on a value that would no longer be a complete checksum.

Nothing is enabled here and nothing is negotiated.  virtio_net_init_instance()
still only records offered(csum=..) and refuses to acknowledge
VIRTIO_NET_F_CSUM / VIRTIO_NET_F_GUEST_CSUM, and NET_DEV_CAP_TX_CSUM_OFFLOAD /
NET_DEV_CAP_RX_CSUM_OFFLOAD stay defined and unset.

docs/net/checksum-offload.md is the investigation: what each required change
would touch (upstream opt.h or lwipopts.h, upstream tcp_out.c, an upstream
pbuf.h per-frame bit, an A20_DRIVER_ABI bump from 2 for the send path),
what breaks if it is half-done, and the order to do it in.  The intent is
registered as DIVERGENCE.md section 2.10, explicitly marked as an intent
rather than an implemented divergence -- there is no code to carry across an
upstream re-sync, only a checklist to re-evaluate.

Every lwIP, QEMU and A20OS line number in the new document was checked
against the tree this commit is built from.

a20: derive the guest address used by the hostfwd rule


tools/targets-smoke.mk carried a note for whoever owned this file: it emits
"tcp::5555-:5555", which QEMU 10 refuses.  Measured on QEMU 10.0.13 here before
changing anything, because the note and the binary may disagree:

  tcp::5555-:5555                              -> Invalid parameter (rejected)
  hostfwd=tcp::5555-:5555=on                   -> starts, binds 5555
  hostfwd=tcp::5555-10.0.2.15:5555=on         -> starts, binds 5555

So the bare form *is* the failure, and the existing `hostfwd=`-prefix rewrite
already fixes it.  The "Missing guest address" message the note quotes does not
appear on this QEMU for any of these spellings -- the string exists in the
binary, but the -netdev user path does not reach it.  I could not reproduce that
half of the note, and am not claiming it.

What changes anyway: the derived rule now spells the guest address the way
smoke-netfilter-nat measures as working end to end, instead of relying on QEMU's
default for the guest half.  The default is the address the tree's own boards
boot with under slirp -- a20.ip=10.0.2.15 in
kernel/platform/qemu-virt-x86_64/board.c, and the -append line every target in
tools/targets-smoke.mk uses -- named once as GUEST_ADDR_DEFAULT.

  tcp::2222-:22  ->  hostfwd=tcp::2222-10.0.2.15:22=on

carries `hostfwd=` is passed through untouched; and a shape this function does
not recognise is passed through with the key spelled out rather than rewritten
into a different broken shape, so `a20 check` still gets to report it.  That
last one replaces the old `^(?:tcp|udp):[^-]*-[^:]*:\d+$` test, which matched by
prefix shape and could not tell an empty guest address from a present one.

parse_hostfwd_ports() in tools/a20_resource.py is untouched: it reads the
manifest form, where the guest address is legitimately optional, so the preflight
keeps reporting the host ports an instance claims.

A separate PI-futex probe reproducibly changes the parent's COW-shared word (20/20) while its control stays clean, confirming that the PI path's raw physical-frame write bypasses COW. Record a fix plan to break COW before mapping the word, preserving the atomic store; the bug is not yet fixed here.

docs/graphics: distinguish Minecraft window creation from XWayland presentation

A validated X11 interposer shows that Minecraft creates/maps no X window even when its GL path reaches the menu or sound startup; a working `glxgears` control does create and map a window, but X11 windows still are not presented. Thus there are two separate issues: Minecraft/GLFW window creation and XWayland/wlroots presentation. DISPLAY-unset runs load Wayland libraries but stall before window creation, so the Wayland path is not yet a workaround.

mm: fix MCS handoff and run the anonymous status fast path without mm->lock

Serve pre-provisioned anonymous faults through `mm_fault_from_status()` before taking the global `mm->lock`, falling back when provisioning is unavailable. The contention work exposed two MCS handoff defects: unlock used shared node state and did not reliably wake the next waiter. Record the corrected handoff and P5 status; the commit reports non-vacuous SMP=8 smokes and three-architecture builds.
messages.reason: 最终实现提交：概括P5 fast path及真实MCS交接修复，保留消息给出的SMP、多架构和非空洞计数证据。

Keep `MM_LOCK_MODEL` as the transitional contract and carve out only the status fast path, which relies on per-address node locking; ordinary COW/file/VMA installs remain under `mm->lock`. Add the reverse metadata-to-VMA audit (`vmai`) alongside the existing PTE-to-metadata walk, assert `vmai=0` in `smoke-mm-pt-race`, and document why `smoke-mm-stress` does not cover it.

messages.message:
docs: close P6/P7 as blocked on the status metadata format

The status byte can classify faults but cannot carry the vnode/fd/offset data needed for file and COW servicing; brk pages are not provisioned with status either, leaving no implementable P6 subset. P7 also cannot remove `PTE_SWAP` until swap payload storage is redesigned: the payload is 44 bits on 64-bit targets and 24 bits on 32-bit targets. Correct the UFFD attribution: the fast-path safety bit is status-driven, while the VMA range table remains authoritative for unregister races. Documentation only.
